requirements.title: Expressions are formed from operands, operators, and parentheses
requirements.definition: The overall expression syntax is built from operands, operators, and parentheses. Operands are scalar or array, operations are intrinsic or defined, and an operand may itself be an expression. The detailed grammar, operator applicability, and interpretation are owned by the following subclauses.

pending.operand-operator-parenthesis-form: PENDING positive-control source shape with a parenthesized arithmetic expression (2+3) assigned to an integer result. The oracle is literal 5 and reached assignment, making the use of operands, operator, and parentheses non-vacuous while the precise grammar is credited to R1001/R1007.
pending.scalar-operand: PENDING positive-control source shape with two scalar integer operands and a literal result oracle. Both operands are assigned distinct literals before use so the observation is not merely constant folding.
pending.array-operand: PENDING positive-control source shape with two rank-one integer array operands and expected literal array result. The oracle is shape [2] and element values, with conformability and elemental semantics cited to 10.1.10.
pending.intrinsic-operation: PENDING positive-control source shape using an intrinsic add-op on integers and checking literal 9. The plan must avoid a user-defined OPERATOR interface so the operation kind is not ambiguous.
pending.defined-operation: PENDING positive-control source shape with an explicit generic OPERATOR(.combine.) interface whose function returns a literal-distinguishable result. The oracle is the function's specified literal result after reached execution; interface validity and interpretation remain 15.4.3.4.2 and 10.1.6 dependencies.
pending.nested-expression-operand: PENDING positive-control source shape using (1+2)*(3+4) and comparing with literal 21. The nested subexpressions have separate literal expectations, ensuring the nesting is observed rather than only final assignment syntax.

requirements.oracle: Future controls should use literal result checks and minimal expression shapes, while assigning actual grammar credit to the numbered rules in 10.1.2.2-10.1.2.9 and semantic credit to 10.1.3-10.1.12.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Numbered syntax rules and constraints carry the 4.2 diagnostic-capability duty, but future negative plans must isolate the cited rule or constraint and must not rely on compiler agreement, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted code, undefined reads, or interpretation and evaluation rules owned by 10.1.3-10.1.12.

requirements.title: Expression grammar uses primary and level-1 through level-5 categories
requirements.definition: An expression is defined using the categories primary, level-1 expression, level-2 expression, level-3 expression, level-4 expression, and level-5 expression. Each category's exact syntax remains with its defining rule.

pending.primary-category: PENDING positive-control source shape using a literal constant primary with literal oracle. The future case attributes only category admission to this facet; literal syntax remains Clause 7.
pending.level-1-category: PENDING positive-control source shape using a defined unary operator on a primary with a literal-distinguishable function result. The oracle is the function result literal, and defined operator interface validity remains 15.4.3.4.2.
pending.level-2-category: PENDING positive-control source shape using numeric add/multiply/power with literal integer oracle and parentheses avoided except where needed to isolate the category. R1005-R1010 own detailed credit.
pending.level-3-category: PENDING positive-control source shape using character concatenation with literal string oracle. Character operand interpretation remains 10.1.5.3.
pending.level-4-category: PENDING positive-control source shape using a relational operator with a logical literal oracle and an alternate branch proving execution. Relational interpretation remains 10.1.5.5.
pending.level-5-category: PENDING positive-control source shape using .AND. or .EQV. with a logical literal oracle. Logical operation interpretation remains 10.1.5.4.

requirements.oracle: Each future plan should name the specific defining rule for the category under observation and use an independent literal result to make the category use non-vacuous.

requirements.title: Expression categories correspond to precedence levels and bottom out at primary
requirements.definition: The expression categories are tied to operator precedence, are generally defined in terms of other categories, and have primary as the simplest form of each category. This is the structural summary for the precedence ladder, not an interpretation rule.

pending.precedence-ladder: PENDING positive-control source shapes covering the full precedence chain as separate, attributable steps: primary, defined unary, power **, multiply/divide, unary add/subtract, binary add/subtract, concatenation, one relation, .NOT., .AND., .OR., .EQV./.NEQV., and defined binary. Each statement isolates one step with a literal oracle where that step is value-observable; associative layers such as //, .AND., and .EQV./.NEQV. retain explicit unobservable-pending facets under their owning rules rather than pretending that value distinguishes grouping.
pending.recursive-category-definition: PENDING positive-control source shape with nested expressions such as ((1+2)*3)==9 and a logical literal oracle. The plan cites each owning category rule instead of assigning all credit to this prose summary.
pending.primary-as-simplest-form: PENDING positive-control source shape using a single literal primary in contexts requiring level-1 through expr via the grammar chain, with literal value oracle. Non-vacuity comes from using the same primary in at least two higher-level contexts with distinct expected results.
